title: Manual lensometer (focimeter)
caption: A lensometer neutralizes a spectacle lens to read its back vertex power, cylinder axis, prism and add, and is used to mark optical centers before edging.
author: Janee
credit: Janee / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Automated lensmeter
caption: An automated lensmeter reads sphere, cylinder, axis and prism electronically, but the lens must still be positioned with the back surface against the lens stop.
author: Phoropter99
credit: Phoropter99 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Lens clock (Geneva lens measure)
caption: A lens clock measures surface curvature by sagitta and is calibrated for index 1.53, so readings on other materials must be converted to true power.
author: Frank Eichler
credit: Frank Eichler / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Lens clock principle diagram
caption: The two fixed outer pins and the movable center pin measure the sagitta of a surface, which the dial converts to dioptric surface power.
author: StationNT5Bmedia and Srleffler
credit: StationNT5Bmedia and Srleffler / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Corneal-reflex pupillometer
caption: A corneal-reflex pupillometer measures binocular and monocular PD by aligning a hairline with each corneal light reflex, at distance or near fixation.
author: Issa not
credit: Issa not / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Phoropter (refractor)
caption: A phoropter holds spherical and cylindrical trial lenses, prisms and a Jackson cross cylinder used to determine the refraction that becomes the spectacle Rx.
author: Phoropter99
credit: Phoropter99 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Progressive addition lens in a frame
caption: A progressive addition lens has no visible segment line; power increases gradually down the corridor from distance to the full near add.
author: Stanistani
credit: Stanistani / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Progressive lens clear and distorted zones
caption: Progressive lenses have unwanted peripheral astigmatism (gray) on either side of the corridor; harder designs have narrower, more intense blur zones.
author: Hold2file (English Wikipedia)
credit: Hold2file (English Wikipedia) / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain

title: Lined bifocal spectacles
caption: A lined bifocal has a visible near segment; seg height is normally fit at or slightly below the lower lid margin.
author: Frank C. Müller, Baden-Baden
credit: Frank C. Müller, Baden-Baden / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Executive (Franklin) bifocal lens blank
caption: An executive bifocal's segment spans the full lens width with a straight ledge line, giving the widest near field but a heavier, thicker lens.
author: Controldemiopia
credit: Controldemiopia / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Rimless (drill-mount) frame
caption: Rimless mountings attach the bridge and temples directly to drilled lenses, so impact-resistant materials like polycarbonate or Trivex are preferred.
author: Sciencia58
credit: Sciencia58 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Z87+ marked safety eyewear
caption: ANSI Z87.1 safety eyewear is marked Z87 (Z87+ for high-impact rated), and prescription safety lenses carry the manufacturer's monogram.
author: Карма2
credit: Карма2 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Polarized vs non-polarized lens test
caption: Two polarized lenses crossed at 90 degrees block transmitted light, a quick check that a sunlens is polarized and its axis is vertical.
author: Keministi
credit: Keministi / Wikimedia Commons, CC0; resized for this app

title: Photochromic lens
caption: Photochromic lenses darken under UV exposure and lighten indoors; most activate poorly behind a car windshield, which blocks UV.
author: Vista Lowcost
credit: Vista Lowcost / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Anti-reflective coating comparison
caption: An uncoated lens (top) shows strong surface reflections, while an AR-coated lens (bottom) uses thin-film interference to cut reflections and leaves a faint residual tint.
author: Justin Lebar
credit: Justin Lebar / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Keratometer
caption: A keratometer measures the radius of curvature of the central cornea (about a 3 mm zone), giving the K readings used to select a contact lens base curve.
author: Mike Blyth
credit: Mike Blyth / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Slit lamp biomicroscope
caption: The slit lamp biomicroscope is the core tool for evaluating contact lens fit, movement and the health of the cornea, conjunctiva and lids.
author: Issa not
credit: Issa not / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Corneal topography map
caption: Corneal topography maps curvature across the whole cornea, with warm colors marking steeper areas and cool colors flatter ones.
author: Jason7825 (English Wikipedia)
credit: Jason7825 (English Wikipedia) / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain

title: Keratoconus on corneal topography
caption: Keratoconus shows as a localized inferior area of steepening on a topography map, often with irregular astigmatism best corrected by rigid or scleral lenses.
author: Elise A. Slim et al.
credit: Elise A. Slim et al. / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0; resized for this app

title: Soft (silicone hydrogel) contact lens
caption: Silicone hydrogel soft lenses combine silicone for high oxygen permeability (Dk) with hydrogel for wettability and comfort.
author: David McClenaghan, CSIRO
credit: David McClenaghan, CSIRO / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0; resized for this app

title: Soft contact lens on the eye
caption: A soft lens is larger than the cornea and should cover it fully with the edge resting on the conjunctiva beyond the limbus.
author: Reinhard Müller
credit: Reinhard Müller / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Rigid gas permeable (RGP) contact lens
caption: A rigid gas permeable lens is smaller than the cornea and masks corneal astigmatism with a tear lens, here designed for keratoconus.
author: BillC (English Wikipedia)
credit: BillC (English Wikipedia) / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain

title: Reverse-geometry orthokeratology lens
caption: An orthokeratology lens uses reverse geometry, a flat center with a steeper reverse curve, to temporarily flatten the central cornea overnight to reduce myopia.
author: Antonio Calossi
credit: Antonio Calossi / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Scleral contact lens
caption: A scleral lens vaults completely over the cornea and rests on the sclera, holding a fluid reservoir useful for irregular corneas and severe dry eye.
author: L8rgator
credit: L8rgator / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: 1950s contact lens vs 1990s contact lens
caption: Early contact lenses were rigid PMMA with essentially no oxygen permeability; modern lenses use gas permeable or hydrogel materials.
author: Bienengasse
credit: Bienengasse / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Fluorescein staining under cobalt blue light
caption: Sodium fluorescein pools in areas of epithelial loss and glows green under the slit lamp's cobalt blue filter, revealing corneal abrasions and staining.
author: James Heilman, MD
credit: James Heilman, MD / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Corneal neovascularization
caption: Chronic corneal hypoxia from low-Dk lenses or overwear can drive blood vessels to grow from the limbus into the normally avascular cornea.
author: Etung1
credit: Etung1 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Contact lens related corneal ulcer
caption: A contact lens related corneal ulcer is a sight-threatening infection; the patient must stop lens wear and be seen urgently by an eye doctor.
author: Iceclanl
credit: Iceclanl / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Acanthamoeba keratitis
caption: Acanthamoeba keratitis is linked to exposing lenses to tap water, swimming or hot tubs, and causes pain out of proportion to the findings.
author: Jacob Lorenzo-Morales, Naveed A. Khan, Julia Walochnik
credit: Jacob Lorenzo-Morales, Naveed A. Khan, Julia Walochnik / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0; resized for this app

title: Human eye cross-section diagram
caption: The cornea provides about two-thirds of the eye's refracting power, with the crystalline lens supplying the adjustable remainder through accommodation.
author: Rhcastilhos. And Jmarchn.
credit: Rhcastilhos. And Jmarchn. / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Anterior, posterior and vitreous chambers
caption: Aqueous humor is made by the ciliary body in the posterior chamber, flows through the pupil into the anterior chamber, and drains through the trabecular meshwork.
author: Holly Fischer; vector by Pixelsquid
credit: Holly Fischer; vector by Pixelsquid / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0; resized for this app

title: Anterior chamber angle structures (gonioscopy)
caption: Seen by gonioscopy, the angle shows Schwalbe's line (1), trabecular meshwork (2), scleral spur (3), ciliary body band (4) and iris (5).
author: Snoop
credit: Snoop / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 de; resized for this app

title: Cornea layers (histology)
caption: The cornea's layers from front to back are epithelium, Bowman's layer, stroma, Descemet's membrane and endothelium; the stroma makes up about 90% of its thickness.
author: Henry Vandyke Carter
credit: Henry Vandyke Carter / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain

title: Extraocular muscles
caption: Six extraocular muscles, four recti and two obliques, move each eye; imbalance between them underlies phorias, tropias and prism prescriptions.
author: OpenStax College
credit: OpenStax College / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0; resized for this app

title: Cataract
caption: A cataract is clouding of the crystalline lens, causing glare and blurred vision; after surgery an intraocular lens replaces the natural lens.
author: Rakesh Ahuja, MD
credit: Rakesh Ahuja, MD / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Glaucomatous optic disc cupping
caption: Advanced glaucoma enlarges the optic cup relative to the disc as nerve fibers are lost, producing peripheral visual field loss.
author: Snoop (German Wikipedia)
credit: Snoop (German Wikipedia) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Age-related macular degeneration fundus
caption: Age-related macular degeneration damages the macula and central vision, while peripheral vision is usually preserved.
author: Tmhlee
credit: Tmhlee / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Diabetic retinopathy fundus
caption: Diabetic retinopathy shows hemorrhages, exudates and abnormal vessels in the retina; fluctuating blood sugar can also shift a diabetic patient's refraction.
author: Shaofeng Hao et al.
credit: Shaofeng Hao et al. / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0; resized for this app

title: Pterygium
caption: A pterygium is a wedge of fibrovascular conjunctival tissue growing onto the cornea, linked to UV exposure, and can induce astigmatism.
author: José Miguel Varas, MD
credit: José Miguel Varas, MD / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0; resized for this app

title: Pinguecula
caption: A pinguecula is a yellowish raised deposit on the bulbar conjunctiva near the limbus that, unlike a pterygium, does not grow onto the cornea.
author: Red eye2008
credit: Red eye2008 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; resized for this app

title: Keratoconus (Munson's sign)
caption: In advanced keratoconus the cone pushes the lower lid into a V shape on downgaze, called Munson's sign.
author: William Charles Caccamise, Sr, MD
credit: William Charles Caccamise, Sr, MD / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Allergic conjunctivitis
caption: Allergic conjunctivitis causes itching, redness and conjunctival swelling (chemosis); contact lens wear is usually suspended until it settles.
author: James Heilman, MD
credit: James Heilman, MD / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized for this app

title: Normal fundus
caption: A normal fundus shows the optic disc with a small central cup, the retinal arteries and veins, and the darker macula with the fovea at its center.
author: Mikael Häggström, M.D.
credit: Mikael Häggström, M.D. / Wikimedia Commons, CC0; resized for this app
